question.text: Which of the following correctly describes the futures pricing model used for each derivative type?

answer.text: Currency futures use Interest Rate Parity (IRP), equity futures use Cost of Carry, and GOI single-bond futures use a no-arbitrage cost-of-carry model (cash price plus financing cost minus income on the cash position)
All three types use the same Cost of Carry model with identical inputs
Currency and equity futures use IRP while bond futures use the Black-Scholes model
Bond futures use Cost of Carry, currency futures use duration-based pricing, and equity futures use IRP

explanation.text: The Logic: Currency futures: F = S × (1 + R_domestic × t) / (1 + R_foreign × t) — Interest Rate Parity based on the rate differential. Equity futures: F = S × e^((r − q)t) or S × (1 + (r − d) × t) — Cost of Carry net of dividend yield. Single bond futures (e.g., GOI single-bond contracts): no-arbitrage cash price plus financing cost minus income (coupon) earned on the cash position. The Trap: All three are no-arbitrage models, but the inputs differ. Conversion factors and the notional-bond yield basket are settlement/product-design features used for notional-bond futures and the deliverable set — they are not the general futures pricing model for a single underlying. Note: Cross-asset comparison: IRP uses two interest rates, equity Cost of Carry uses the risk-free rate net of dividends, and bond futures pricing relies on financing cost net of coupon income on the deliverable cash bond.
